definition_zh: 告诉；讲述；吩咐；分辨；告发；显示；数；产生效果
definition_en: to give information by speech or writing, to narrate a story, to order someone to do something, or to be able to distinguish one thing from another
core_image: 一个人凑近另一个人的耳朵，话从口中流出
scene: 夜里孩子缠着母亲讲故事，母亲点了一盏小灯。Grandmother told them a tale of the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 tell 是「讲述」（第 2 个义项：说出故事的内容）；句意：祖母给孩子们讲了一个大海的故事。

pos.zh: 告发；产生效果；（语言）显示

derivatives.zh: 讲述者；银行出纳员（由 tell 加表人后缀构成，指说话或点钞的人）
有说服力的；起作用的（现在分词转形容词，指话语产生效果）
算命者（复合词，tell 保留「预示、说出」义）

senses.title: Give information by speaking
senses.definition: to give information to someone in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用口头或书面方式把信息告诉某人
senses.example: Tell me your address and I will send the parcel.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的地址告诉我，我把包裹寄出去。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply putting something into words for another person: speech is counted out to a listener.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是把某事用话点给别人听：话语像被「数给」听者。

senses.title: Narrate a story or events
senses.definition: to give an account of a story, or of events in order
senses.definitionCN: 依次讲出故事或事情的经过
senses.example: The grandmother told a tale of the old village.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母讲了一个老村庄的故事。
senses.why: Narration is information stretched into sequence: many small bits of telling are lined up into a whole.
senses.whyCN: 叙述是把信息拉长成序列：许多细小的「告知」连成整体，便成了故事。

senses.title: Order someone to do something
senses.definition: to say to someone that they must do something
senses.definitionCN: 要求或指示某人必须做某事
senses.example: The coach told us to warm up first.
senses.exampleCN: 教练吩咐我们先热身。
senses.why: Speech directed at someone becomes instruction; the telling carries weight, not just information.
senses.whyCN: 话语指向某人时就成了指令；此时的「说」带有分量，不只是传递信息。

senses.title: Distinguish one thing from another
senses.definition: to be able to know or judge the difference between things
senses.definitionCN: 能看出或判断出事物之间的差别
senses.example: I cannot tell the twins apart.
senses.exampleCN: 我分辨不出这对双胞胎。
senses.why: To tell here is to reckon or count out a difference, an old sense of counting that survives in judgment.
senses.whyCN: 此义里的 tell 是「点算」出差别——这是它古老的「数、计」义残留在判断里。

senses.title: Reveal an effect or a state
senses.definition: to show or reveal something, especially strain or age, without words
senses.definitionCN: 无需言语就显露出状况，尤指疲累或年岁
senses.example: The long journey was beginning to tell on his health.
senses.exampleCN: 长途跋涉开始影响他的健康。
senses.why: A state that cannot be hidden is itself telling: facts speak when people stay silent.
senses.whyCN: 藏不住的状态自己在「说话」：人不开口时，事实替他开口，便是 tell。

senses.title: Inform against someone
senses.definition: to report someone secretly to a person in authority
senses.definitionCN: 暗中向掌权者举报某人
senses.example: The boy was afraid his classmate would tell on him.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩怕同学告他的状。
senses.why: Telling takes a dark turn when the listener is authority: the same speech act becomes betrayal.
senses.whyCN: 当听话者变成权威，讲述就转向阴暗面：同一个说话动作成了告发。

senses.title: Count things one by one
senses.definition: to count objects or recite numbers in order, now mainly in fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 逐一清点或顺次念数，今多见于固定短语
senses.example: The old phrase tells the beads one by one.
senses.exampleCN: 旧短语里一颗颗数念珠。
senses.why: This is the root sense: tell once meant simply to count, as it still does in teller and all told.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根义：tell 原本就是「数」，至今还活在 teller 与 all told 里。

intro.en: Tell is a native Germanic verb. Its oldest meaning is to count or reckon, from which telling others and telling stories both grew.
intro.cn: tell 是日耳曼本族动词，最古老的含义是「数、点算」，告知与讲故事都由此长出。

items.en: Tellan meant to count, reckon, or enumerate things one by one.
items.cn: 古英语 tellan 意为逐个清点、计算。

items.en: Talu, the related noun, gave both tale and tally, keeping the counting sense.
items.cn: 同源名词 talu 衍生出 tale 与 tally，保留了「数」义。

items.en: The verb goes back to a Germanic root for counting, cognate with German zählen.
items.cn: 动词可追溯至日耳曼语「计数」词根，与德语 zählen 同源。

items.en: The sense moved from counting things to counting out words: informing, narrating and ordering.
items.cn: 词义从「数物」移向「数话」：告知、叙述与吩咐相继出现。

items.en: Judging differences and revealing effects kept the reckoning image, while counting survives only in old phrases.
items.cn: 分辨与显效保留了「点算」意象，而「数」义只留在旧短语中。

note.en: Tell is set beside its Germanic relatives and beside speech verbs that overlap with it.
note.cn: 把 tell 与日耳曼同族词，以及与之交叠的言语动词放在一起对比。

entries.definition: a story, from the same Germanic counting root
entries.definitionCN: 故事；与 tell 同出「计数」词根
计数；记录，保留「点算」古义

entries.definition: a person who tells, or counts money at a bank
to speak words, without the sense of informing a particular person
entries.definitionCN: 说出话来，不含「告知特定对象」的意味

entries.definition: to give a spoken account of events in order
entries.definitionCN: 依次口述事件经过，更书面

entries.definition: to give someone facts, often official

normalIntro.en: Real links: the counting root, the tale family, the bank teller, and the phrase all told.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：计数词根、tale 词族、银行出纳与 all told 短语。

normal.en: Tell once meant to count; all told still means counted altogether.
normal.cn: tell 原义是数；all told 至今意为「总计清点」。

normal.en: Tale and tell are twins: a tale is something told.
normal.cn: tale 与 tell 是孪生兄弟：故事就是被讲述的东西。

normal.en: A bank teller literally counts money for you.
normal.cn: 银行出纳员 teller 字面上就是替你数钱的人。

normal.en: Tell the twins apart: count out the difference between them.
normal.cn: tell the twins apart：把两人之间的差别「点算」出来。

normal.en: Tell on him: your words reach the teacher, and the counting turns into blame.
normal.cn: tell on him：你的话传到老师那里，「点算」变成了指责。

abstract.en: Every sentence is a small counting: word after word handed to a listener.
abstract.cn: 每句话都是一次小小的清点：一个词接一个词递给听者。

abstract.en: Silence also tells: what cannot be hidden speaks by itself.
abstract.cn: 沉默也会说话：藏不住的东西自己开口。

abstract.en: Stories are counted-out time, bead after bead.
abstract.cn: 故事是被一颗颗数出的时光。

examples.en: She told me the truth about the missing key.
examples.cn: 她把钥匙失踪的真相告诉了我。

examples.en: Grandfather told the same story every winter night.
examples.cn: 祖父每年冬夜都讲同一个故事。

examples.en: The strain of the exams is telling on her.
examples.cn: 考试的压力正在影响她。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太欧」——太欧（tel）老师一遍遍数着欧几里得的题，数着数着就讲给你听 → tell 数、讲、告诉

root: 日耳曼本族动词：古英语 tellan「数、点算」，同根名词 talu 给出 tale 与 tally；「告知、讲述」由「逐一数出」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: From counting things, tell grew into counting out words to a listener, and finally into silent facts that speak.
sensesIntro.cn: tell 从数物出发，长出向听者「数话」的告知与讲述，最终连无声的事实也会 tell。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: counting things out one by one, then counting out words.
core.cn: 核心意象：逐一点数，再逐词「点数」给听者。

branches.en: The root sense survives in old phrases.
branches.cn: 词根义存活于旧短语。

branches.en: Information handed over word by word.
branches.cn: 信息被逐词递交。

branches.en: Many tellings lined up become a story.
branches.cn: 许多次讲述连缀成故事。

branches.en: Speech aimed at a person turns to order or to betrayal.
branches.cn: 指向某人的话语变成命令或告发。

branches.en: Reckoning a difference; facts that speak unbidden.
branches.cn: 点算差别；事实不请自言。

intro.en: Tell belongs to the Germanic counting family shared with tale, tally and talk.
intro.cn: tell 属日耳曼「计数」词族，与 tale、tally、talk 同源相关。

latinIntro.en: Tell is not from Latin; the nearest Latin parallels are reckoning verbs, given here only as contrast.
latinIntro.cn: tell 并非源自拉丁语；此处列出拉丁语中的「计算」动词仅作对照。

items.exampleCN: talu 衍生 tale 与 tally。

items.meaningCN: 数；计算（拉丁来源的对照词）

definition_en: a measure of how hot or cold something is
core_image: 墙上的温度计里，红色液柱停在一个刻度上，室内外差出一大截
scene: 实验室墙上的温度计显示，室内比室外高许多。The thermometer showed a temperature ten degrees higher indoors.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「可测量的冷热程度」（第 1 个义项：温度读数）；句意为温度计显示室内温度比室外高十度。

senses.title: A measured degree of heat
senses.definition: a number expressing how hot or cold a body or space is
senses.definitionCN: 表示物体或空间冷热程度的数值
senses.example: The thermometer showed a temperature ten degrees higher indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 温度计显示室内温度比室外高十度。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'a tempering or moderation'; early science used it for the balance of hot and cold in a body, then for the measured balance itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「调和、适度」；早期科学用它指体内冷热的平衡，后来指被测出的这个平衡。

senses.title: Body heat
senses.definition: the internal heat of a living body, normally around thirty-seven degrees
senses.definitionCN: 活体内部的温度，正常约三十七度
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's temperature twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每天记录病人两次体温。
senses.why: A living body regulates its own balance of heat, which is exactly what the old sense of tempering described.
senses.whyCN: 活体自行调节冷热平衡，这正是旧义「调和」所描述的。

senses.title: The weather figure
senses.definition: the outdoor air temperature reported in a forecast
senses.definitionCN: 预报中报告的室外空气温度
senses.example: The forecast gives a temperature of minus five tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 预报说今晚气温为零下五度。
senses.why: Air is a body too, and meteorology applies the same measurement to the atmosphere.
senses.whyCN: 空气也是一种物体，气象学把同一测量用到大气上。

senses.title: A fever
senses.definition: an abnormally high body temperature caused by illness
senses.definitionCN: 疾病引起的异常升高的体温
senses.example: The child has a temperature and should stay home.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子发烧了，应该待在家里。
senses.why: In everyday speech a 'temperature' means the raised figure, not the normal one, so the measurement stands for the illness.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语中 a temperature 指升高的那个数值，而不是正常值，于是测量结果代表了疾病。

senses.title: A device set point
senses.definition: the target temperature set on a thermostat or oven
senses.definitionCN: 在恒温器或烤箱上设定的目标温度
senses.example: Set the temperature to two hundred degrees before baking.
senses.exampleCN: 烘烤前把温度设为两百度。
senses.why: A control dial turns the noun into an instruction: the temperature is what the machine is told to reach.
senses.whyCN: 控制旋钮把这个名词变成指令：温度是机器被要求达到的值。

senses.title: The emotional climate
senses.definition: the general mood or level of tension in a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中的总体情绪或紧张程度
senses.example: The temperature of the debate rose after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 声明发布后，辩论的火气升高了。
senses.why: Social heat is read like physical heat: a room can become hot with anger.
senses.whyCN: 社会的热像物理的热一样被读取：一个房间可以因愤怒而变热。

senses.title: A physical quantity
senses.definition: in physics, a property measuring the average kinetic energy of particles
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中衡量粒子平均动能的属性
senses.example: The temperature of the gas rises as the piston compresses it.
senses.exampleCN: 活塞压缩气体时，气体温度升高。
senses.why: Physics narrows the everyday number to a precise property of a system.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把日常数字收窄为系统的精确属性。

senses.title: A standard condition
senses.definition: the ordinary indoor heat at which materials and reactions are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较材料与反应时所用的通常室内温度
senses.example: Store the reagent at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 把试剂存放在室温下。
senses.why: Labs need a standard, so 'room temperature' becomes a fixed benchmark rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 实验室需要一个标准，于是「室温」成了固定基准而不是描述。

intro.en: Temperature comes from Latin temperatura 'a tempering, a due mixture'. The modern physical sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: temperature 出自拉丁语 temperatura「调和、适当的混合」。现代物理义是后来的收窄。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Temperatura meant a mixing in due proportion, from temperare 'to mix, regulate, restrain'.
items.cn: temperatura 意为按适当比例混合，出自 temperare「混合、调节、节制」。

items.en: Temperare is related to tempus 'time, season', because mixing in the right measure was imagined as keeping to the right season.
items.cn: temperare 与 tempus「时间、季节」相关，因为「按正确比例混合」被想象为顺应正确的时令。

items.en: Medieval medicine used temperatura for the balanced mixture of humours in a body, and English borrowed it as temperature in this medical sense.
items.cn: 中世纪医学用 temperatura 指体内体液的有序混合，英语借入时也带这一医学义。

items.en: With the thermometer, the word shifted from a balance of qualities to a measurable degree of heat.
items.cn: 随着温度计的发明，这个词从「性质的平衡」转为「可测量的热度」。

items.en: Physics fixed temperature as a quantity, and everyday speech kept the special phrase 'have a temperature' for fever.
items.cn: 物理学把 temperature 固定为一个物理量，日常口语则保留 have a temperature 这一说法指发烧。

items.en: Room temperature and body temperature became standard benchmarks in labs, kitchens and clinics.
items.cn: 室温与体温成为实验室、厨房与诊所的标准基准。

note.en: Group one separates the temperament words from the temperature word; group two holds related measures and sensations.
note.cn: 第一组分辨 temperament 词族与 temperature 的区别；第二组是相关度量与感觉词。

entries.definition: A person's usual character; it comes from the same Latin root, where a balance of humours was thought to shape personality.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人惯常的性格；出自同一拉丁词根，古人认为体液平衡塑造性格。

entries.definition: To moderate or to become angry easily; the noun means a state of mind, not a degree of heat.
entries.definitionCN: 使缓和，或指容易发怒；名词指心境，而不是热度。

entries.definition: Relating to time or to the material world; it comes from tempus 'time', not from temperare.
entries.definitionCN: 与时间或世俗世界有关；出自 tempus「时间」，而非 temperare。

entries.definition: The energy transferred by a difference in temperature; heat is the cause, temperature is the measured result.
entries.definitionCN: 因温差而传递的能量；热是原因，温度是被测出的结果。

entries.definition: A raised body temperature caused by illness; it names the condition, while a temperature is just the reading.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病引起的体温升高；它指病况，而 temperature 只是读数。

entries.definition: The figure shown by an instrument; a temperature is one kind of reading.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器显示的数字；温度是读数的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin family is real, and the measuring instruments are real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁词族真实存在，测量仪器也都是真实复合词。

normal.en: temperature and temperament share temperare: one measures the body's heat, the other names the body's mix of moods.
normal.cn: temperature 与 temperament 共享 temperare：一个测身体的热，一个指身体性情的混合。

normal.en: thermometer = thermo- (heat) + -meter (measure), the instrument that reads a temperature.
normal.cn: thermometer = thermo-「热」+ -meter「测量」，读取温度的仪器。

normal.en: thermostat = thermo- + -stat (standing, holding), a device that holds a set temperature.
normal.cn: thermostat = thermo- + -stat「保持」，把温度保持在设定值的装置。

normal.en: room temperature is the standard phrase in recipes and lab protocols for ordinary indoor heat.
normal.cn: room temperature 是食谱与实验规程中表示通常室内温度的标准说法。

normal.en: to have a temperature means to be feverish, because the number has gone above normal.
normal.cn: have a temperature 指发烧，因为那个数字高出了正常值。

abstract.en: Abstractly, temperature is balance made countable: hot and cold are weighed against each other and turned into a number.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，temperature 是可数的平衡：冷与热相互权衡，变成一个数字。

abstract.en: The same number can describe a room, a body, a gas or the mood of a meeting.
abstract.cn: 同一个数字可以描述房间、身体、气体，也可以描述一场会议的气氛。

abstract.en: So temperature is not heat itself but heat made comparable.
abstract.cn: 所以 temperature 不是热本身，而是变得可比较的热。

examples.en: The temperature fell below zero before dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明前气温降到了零下。

examples.en: Keep the oven at a constant temperature.
examples.cn: 让烤箱保持恒温。

examples.en: Her temperature returned to normal after two days.
examples.cn: 两天后她的体温恢复正常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「天不热」：天不热也有温度 → temperature 温度

root: 拉丁语 temperatura「调和、适当混合」← temperare「混合、调节」，与 tempus「时间、季节」相关；十七世纪起经温度计的使用转为可测量的热度。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one measurable balance: a room, a body, the weather, a fever, a thermostat setting, a social mood, a physical quantity and a standard benchmark.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一个可测的平衡展开：房间、身体、天气、发烧、恒温设定、群体情绪、物理量，以及标准基准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hot and cold weighed against each other and read off as a number.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷与热相互权衡，被读成一个数字。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: everyday heat and the physicist's quantity are the same number at two levels of precision.
branches.cn: 测量：日常热度与物理学家的物理量，是同一数字的两种精度。

branches.en: THE BODY: normal warmth and illness-heat are one scale read above and below the usual line.
branches.cn: 身体：正常体温与病热，是同一条刻度在常线上下两侧的读数。

branches.en: THE AIR: a forecast figure and a lab benchmark both describe ordinary surroundings.
branches.cn: 空气：预报数字与实验室基准都在描述平常环境。

branches.en: CONTROL: a dial turns the noun into a target to be reached.
branches.cn: 控制：旋钮把这个名词变成一个要达到的目标。

branches.en: MOOD: a room heated by anger borrows the same thermometer.
branches.cn: 情绪：被愤怒加热的房间借用了同一支温度计。

intro.en: Temperature belongs to the Latin temperare family. English adds -ature for the noun, while Greek thermo- supplies the instruments.
intro.cn: temperature 属于拉丁 temperare 词族。英语加 -ature 构成名词，希腊语 thermo- 则提供仪器名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries below are the recorded ancestors of the family; tempus 'time' is included because temperare was built on the idea of the right season.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁条目是该词族有记录的祖先；列出 tempus「时间」，因为 temperare 建立在「合宜时令」的观念上。

items.meaningCN: 读取温度的仪器（thermo- 表示热，-meter 表示测量）
items.exampleCN: 温度计读数是三十八度。

items.meaning: a device that keeps a set temperature
items.meaningCN: 把温度保持在设定值的装置（-stat 表示保持）
items.example: The thermostat switches the heater off.

items.meaning: to moderate; also a state of mind
items.example: She tempered her criticism with praise.
The temperate zone has four seasons.

items.meaning: kept at a fixed heat by a device
items.example: The samples sit in a temperature-controlled room.

items.meaning: the ordinary indoor heat, used as a benchmark
items.meaningCN: 通常的室内温度，用作基准
items.example: Serve the cheese at room temperature.

items.meaning: the internal heat of a living body
items.example: Body temperature is lowest before dawn.

latinEntries.meaning: to mix in due proportion, regulate

definition_zh: 临时的；暂时的；短期的；非永久的；临时工（名词，常用复数）
definition_en: lasting only for a limited time; intended to be used or kept for a short period
core_image: 工地入口立着一块临时围挡，风一吹就晃，却已经立了三年
scene: 搬进新家前，他们先住进一间小公寓。They stayed in a temporary flat while the new house was being painted, and moved out as soon as the work was finished.
sceneCN: 这里 temporary 是「临时的、暂时的」（第 1 个义项：只持续有限时间）；句意：新房刷漆期间他们住在一间临时公寓，一完工就搬走了。图中可辨识物件：简易公寓、纸箱、未拆封的家具、装修中的新房、搬家货车。

pos.zh: 临时工；临时事物（常用复数）

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）

senses.title: Lasting a short time
senses.definition: lasting only for a limited period, not forever
senses.definitionCN: 只持续有限时段，不会永远
senses.example: They found temporary shelter under a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在桥下找到临时遮蔽。
senses.why: Temporary is defined by an end. It does not say how short the period is, only that a limit exists and is expected to arrive.
senses.whyCN: temporary 由“终点”定义。它不说时段多短，只说存在一个被预期会到来的界限。

senses.title: Not permanent
senses.definition: not intended to last or to be final
senses.definitionCN: 不打算长久保留或成为最终状态
senses.example: The agreement is temporary and will be reviewed.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议是暂时的，将会复审。
senses.why: The word often carries a promise or a warning: this state is provisional, so do not build your life on it, or do not despair of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常带承诺或警告：此状态是暂定的，故不要把生活建在其上，也别为它绝望。

senses.title: Of a short-term job
senses.definition: of work or a post that ends after a fixed period
senses.definitionCN: 有固定期限、到期即止的工作或职位
senses.example: She took a temporary job for the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了份暑期临时工作。
senses.why: Labour markets use temporary as a category: the contract has an end date, and with it fewer rights and less security.
senses.whyCN: 劳动力市场把 temporary 当作类别：合同有终止日，随之而来的是更少的权利与保障。

senses.title: Of short-term lodging
senses.definition: of accommodation used until something permanent is available
senses.definitionCN: 在永久住处可用之前使用的住所
senses.example: The family stayed in temporary housing after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾后这家人住进临时住房。
senses.why: Housing makes the word concrete: a roof that is known to be borrowed, often provided by an agency or a friend, and marked by boxes not yet unpacked.
senses.whyCN: 住房把词变具体：一个明知是借来的屋顶，常由机构或朋友提供，以尚未拆封的纸箱为标志。

senses.title: A temporary worker (noun)
senses.definition: a person employed for a limited period, often through an agency
senses.definitionCN: 受雇有限期限的人，常经中介
senses.example: The hospital hired temporaries for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 医院为冬季雇了临时工。
senses.why: The noun turns the adjective into a person. 'Temps' is the clipped, everyday form; the plural temporaries is more formal.
senses.whyCN: 名词把形容词变成人。口语缩略为 temp；复数 temporaries 更正式。

senses.title: A stopgap measure
senses.definition: an arrangement used to solve a problem until a better one is possible
senses.definitionCN: 在更好办法出现前用来解决问题的安排
senses.example: The ban is a temporary measure, not a policy.
senses.exampleCN: 该禁令是权宜之计，而非政策。
senses.why: A temporary measure admits its own inadequacy. It buys time, and the honest ones say so rather than pretending to be final.
senses.whyCN: 权宜之计承认自身不足。它买时间，诚实者会明说，而不假装是最终方案。

senses.title: A temporary file
senses.definition: a computer file created for a short task and deleted later
senses.definitionCN: 为短期任务创建、随后删除的计算机文件
senses.example: The installer left temporary files on the disk.
senses.exampleCN: 安装程序在磁盘上留下了临时文件。
senses.why: Computing literalises the word: the file exists only while a process runs, and its deletion is part of its design.
senses.whyCN: 计算把词字面化：文件只在进程运行时存在，其删除是设计的一部分。

senses.title: A short stay
senses.definition: a visit or residence lasting only a while
senses.definitionCN: 只持续一段时日的访问或居住
senses.example: He made a temporary stay in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他在城里作短期停留。
senses.why: Travel and diplomacy use the word for presence that is explicitly not settlement. The visitor is in place but not of it.
senses.whyCN: 旅行与外交用该词指明确不落户的存在。访客在此地，却不属于此地。

senses.title: A passing setback
senses.definition: a difficulty expected to improve with time
senses.definitionCN: 预期随时间好转的困难
senses.example: The loss was a temporary setback, not a collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 这次亏损是暂时挫折，不是崩溃。
senses.why: Applied to feelings and fortunes, temporary is consolation: it reframes a present pain as a phase with an exit.
senses.whyCN: 用于情绪与境遇时，temporary 是安慰：它把当下的痛重新框定为有出口的阶段。

intro.en: Temporary comes from Latin temporarius, 'of a time, lasting for a time', from tempus 'time' (genitive temporis). English took it in the sixteenth century. The deeper origin of tempus is uncertain; it is often connected with a root meaning 'to stretch or span'.
intro.cn: temporary 出自拉丁语 temporarius“某段时间的、暂时的”，源于 tempus“时间”（属格 temporis）。英语十六世纪借入。tempus 的更早来源不确定，常与表示“伸展、跨度”的词根相连。

items.en: The adjective is first recorded in English in the sense 'lasting only for a time'.
items.cn: 该形容词最早记录于十六世纪四十年代，意为“只持续一段时间的”。

items.en: temporarius means 'of time, belonging to a time, transient', from tempus 'time, season'.
items.cn: temporarius 意为“时间的、属于某时段的、短暂的”，出自 tempus“时间、季节”。

items.en: tempus has the genitive temporis, which is why temporary has an r where the base word seems to lack one.
items.cn: tempus 的属格是 temporis，故 temporary 在词基看似没有 r 的地方出现了一个 r。

items.en: The Indo-European origin of tempus is disputed. A connection with a root meaning 'to stretch, span' is often proposed but not certain.
items.cn: tempus 的印欧来源有争议。常有人提出与表示“伸展、跨度”的词根相关，但并不确定。

items.en: Legal and religious writing spread the word: temporal goods are of this world, temporary arrangements last only a while.
items.cn: 十六世纪法律与宗教写作推广该词：temporal 之物属于此世，temporary 安排只维持一时。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from temp work and temporary housing to temporary files, all sharing an expected end point.
items.cn: 现代用法从临时工作、临时住房到临时文件，皆共享一个预期终点。

note.en: The first group is the tempus family, where r-forms and plain forms alternate; the second is words for shortness of duration, each with a different tone.
note.cn: 第一组是 tempus 词族，r 形式与无 r 形式交替；第二组是表示时短的其他词，语气各异。

entries.definition: the quality of lasting only a while.
relating to time, or to worldly rather than spiritual matters.
entries.definitionCN: 关于时间的；世俗的（非属灵的）。

entries.definition: lasting only a very short time and passing quickly. It is more literary and more absolute than temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 只持续极短时间并迅速消逝。比 temporary 更文学、更绝对。

entries.definition: used or done between two points in time, especially between two official arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: 在两个时点之间、尤在两个正式安排之间使用或做的。

entries.definition: arranged for the present but likely to be changed. It stresses conditionality rather than duration.
entries.definitionCN: 为当下安排但很可能被改。强调条件性而非时长。

normalIntro.en: Real links: tempus/temporis, the r in the English word, the temp-work sense, and the contrast with permanent.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tempus 与 temporis、英语词中的 r、临时工作义，以及同 permanent 的对照。

normal.en: Tempus means time, and its genitive is temporis. That hidden r is why English has temporary.
normal.cn: tempus 意为时间，属格是 temporis。那个藏起来的 r 正是英语 temporary 的来源。

normal.en: Temporary is defined by an end: it does not say how short, only that a stop is expected.
normal.cn: temporary 由终点定义：它不说多短，只说预期会停。

normal.en: A temp job has an end date written into the contract; the word is a legal fact, not just a feeling.
normal.cn: 临时工作的合同里写着终止日；这个词是法律事实，不只是感觉。

normal.en: A temporary file exists only while a process runs; deleting it is part of its design.
normal.cn: 临时文件只在进程运行时存在；删除它是设计的一部分。

normal.en: Temporary vs permanent: one expects an exit, the other expects to remain.
normal.cn: temporary 与 permanent：前者预期出口，后者预期留下。

abstract.en: The temporary is not less real; it is real with a clock attached.
abstract.cn: 临时之物并非不那么真实；它是被系上时钟的真实。

abstract.en: Calling something temporary is a political act: it can make an injustice easier to bear or harder to oppose.
abstract.cn: 把某物称为临时，是一种政治行为：它能让不义更易忍受，也能让它更难被反对。

abstract.en: All arrangements are temporary at some scale; the word only makes the scale visible.
abstract.cn: 一切安排在某个尺度上都是临时的；这个词只是让尺度显现。

examples.en: The museum is closed for temporary repairs.
examples.cn: 博物馆因临时维修闭馆。

examples.en: He took a temporary position at the bank.
examples.cn: 他在银行做了一份临时职位。

examples.en: The decline in sales proved temporary.
examples.cn: 销售下滑被证明是暂时的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摊破若瑞”——摊子破了也别急，若天降祥瑞，很快就能换新的 → temporary 临时的

root: 拉丁语 temporarius“某段时间的、短暂的”，出自 tempus“时间、季节”（属格 temporis）；tempus 的印欧来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of temporary, all marked by an expected end. The end may be a date on a contract, the completion of a house, the closing of a file, or the passing of a mood.
sensesIntro.cn: temporary 的九个义项都以“预期终点”为标记。终点可以是合同日期、房子装完、文件关闭，或情绪过去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a temporary fence that is expected to come down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道预期会被拆掉的临时围挡。

branches.en: DURATION: the word measures a limited span and denies permanence.
branches.cn: 时长：衡量有限跨度，并否认永久。

branches.en: LIFE ARRANGEMENTS: jobs, housing, and the people who fill them are all marked by an end date.
branches.cn: 生活安排：工作、住房与填充其中的人，都带终止日。

branches.en: THE STOPGAP: measures and setbacks are framed as phases with an exit.
branches.cn: 权宜：措施与挫折被框定为有出口的阶段。

branches.en: COMPUTING: the file exists only while needed, and deletion is designed in.
branches.cn: 计算：文件只在需要时存在，删除是设计的一部分。

branches.en: PRESENCE: a short stay is presence without settlement.
branches.cn: 在场：短期停留是“在场而不落户”。

intro.en: Temporary is a Latin adjective in -arius built on the tempus/tempor- stem. English derives -ly and -ness, while the same stem gives temporal, contemporary, tempo, and tempest.
intro.cn: temporary 是建于 tempus/tempor- 词干的拉丁 -arius 形容词。英语派生 -ly 与 -ness，同一词干给出 temporal、contemporary、tempo、tempest。

latinIntro.en: Latin tempus 'time' has the stem tempor-, which supplies temporarius 'lasting a time'. The family includes temporal (of time), contemporary (of the same time), and tempo (time in music). The ultimate origin of tempus is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tempus“时间”的词干为 tempor-，生成 temporarius“持续一段时间的”。词族含 temporal（时间的）、contemporary（同时代的）、tempo（音乐的时间）。tempus 的最终来源不确定。

items.meaningCN: 暂时地；临时地（-ly 副词）
临时性；暂时性（-ness 名词）
时间的；世俗的（-al 形容词）
节拍；速度（同词干，经意大利语）

items.meaning: to act for the moment; to delay
items.meaningCN: 顺应时势；拖延（同词干动词）

definition_zh: 倾向；有…趋势；趋向；照料；照看；管理；在酒吧当班；放牧；（古）侍候
definition_en: to be likely to do something or to move in a certain direction; to take care of someone or something
core_image: 水往低处流，而牧人低头跟着羊群往坡下走
scene: 每到冬天，他的咳嗽就更厉害。Every winter his cough tends to get worse, and the doctor says the cold air is the cause.
sceneCN: 这里 tend 是「倾向于、有…趋势」（第 1 个义项：经常如此或很可能如此）；句意：每年冬天他的咳嗽都倾向于加重，医生说是冷空气刺激。图中可辨识物件：病历、冬季窗景、雾化器、围巾、医生的听诊器。

pos.zh: 倾向；趋向；照料；照看；管理；当班

derivatives.zh: 照料者；温柔的（同根近亲，义已分化）

senses.title: Be likely to do something
senses.definition: to be likely to do or be something, as a regular pattern
senses.definitionCN: 经常如此或很可能如此
senses.example: People tend to ignore warnings they hear too often.
senses.exampleCN: 人们倾向于忽略听太多的警告。
senses.why: Tendere means 'to stretch'. The modern sense pictures behaviour stretched toward one outcome: the pattern leans, and prediction follows the lean.
senses.whyCN: tendere 意为“伸展”。现代义把行为想象为朝某个结果伸展：模式倾斜，预测随倾斜而来。

senses.title: Take care of someone
senses.definition: to look after a person, especially one who is ill or young
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人，尤指病者或幼者
senses.example: Nurses tended the wounded through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 护士整夜照料伤员。
senses.why: This sense has a different parent: it is a shortened form of attend, 'to direct one's mind to'. Care is attention made practical.
senses.whyCN: 此义另有来源：它是 attend“把心思朝向”的缩略。照料是“注意”被付诸实践。

senses.title: Move in a direction
senses.definition: to move or point toward a place or state
senses.definitionCN: 朝某处或某状态移动、指向
senses.example: The path tends toward the river.
senses.exampleCN: 小径趋向河边。
senses.why: The spatial sense is the most literal: a line or a road stretches in a direction. Inclination in behaviour is this stretching made mental.
senses.whyCN: 空间义最字面：一条线或路朝某方向伸展。行为上的倾向，就是这种伸展被心智化。

senses.title: Have an inclination of opinion
senses.definition: to be inclined to hold a view or favour an option
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于持有某观点或支持某选项
senses.example: The committee tends toward a compromise.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会倾向于妥协。
senses.why: Opinions also lean. The verb lets a speaker report a drift without claiming a fixed position: the group is not there yet, but it is tending there.
senses.whyCN: 观点也会倾斜。动词让说话者报告一种漂移而不宣称固定立场：群体尚未到达，但正朝那里去。

senses.title: Look after a fire or machine
senses.definition: to keep a fire, machine, or process working properly
senses.definitionCN: 使炉火、机器或过程正常运转
senses.example: He tended the furnace all night.
senses.exampleCN: 他整夜照看炉子。
senses.why: Tending a fire is maintenance as attention: add fuel, watch the draft, respond to changes. The cared-for object is not alive, but it needs vigilance.
senses.whyCN: 照看炉火是“注意”式的维护：添燃料、看通风、应对变化。被照看之物并非活物，却需要警觉。

senses.title: Serve in a bar
senses.definition: to work behind a bar, serving drinks
senses.definitionCN: 在吧台后工作、供应饮品
senses.example: She tends bar on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 她周末在酒吧当班。
senses.why: American English uses tend for a workplace one keeps running. The bartender tends the bar as a shepherd tends a flock: presence plus upkeep.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语用 tend 指维持一个工作场所运转。酒吧侍者 tend 吧台，如牧人 tend 羊群：在场加维护。

senses.title: Herd animals
senses.definition: to watch over animals as they graze
senses.definitionCN: 看管吃草的牲畜
senses.example: A boy tended the goats on the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 一个男孩在山坡上放羊。
senses.why: Herding is the oldest care sense: the animals move, and the herder's attention moves with them, keeping them from straying.
senses.whyCN: 放牧是最古老的照料义：牲畜移动，牧人的注意力随之前移，防止它们走失。

senses.title: Attend or wait upon (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to attend on a person of rank
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：随侍地位高者
senses.example: The squire tended his lord.
senses.exampleCN: 侍从随侍他的领主。
senses.why: This is the attend branch in its full feudal form: standing ready, mind directed toward the master's needs. Modern care kept the service and dropped the rank.
senses.whyCN: 这是 attend 一支的完整封建形态：立于一旁待命，心思朝向主人的需要。现代“照料”保留服侍，丢掉等级。

senses.title: Converge on a result
senses.definition: of numbers or processes, to approach a limit or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 数字或过程逼近某一极限或结果
senses.example: Under these rules, costs tend toward zero.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些规则下，成本趋于零。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the spatial lean for convergence: a sequence stretches toward a limit it may never reach exactly.
senses.whyCN: 数学用空间倾斜表示收敛：序列朝一个可能永远不能精确到达的极限伸展。

intro.en: English has two tend verbs that now look alike. The 'incline' tend comes from Old French tendre, Latin tendere 'to stretch'. The 'care for' tend is a shortened form of attend, from Old French atendre, Latin attendere 'to give heed'. They merged in spelling but not in origin.
intro.cn: 英语有两个现已形似的 tend 动词。“倾向”的 tend 出自古法语 tendre、拉丁 tendere“伸展”；“照料”的 tend 是 attend 的缩略，出自古法语 atendre、拉丁 attendere“留心”。它们在拼写上合并，来源却不同。

items.en: The 'stretch, incline' verb enters English from Old French tendre, used of movement and direction.
items.cn: “伸展、倾向”动词十三世纪自法语 tendre 进入英语，用于移动与方向。

items.en: tendere means 'to stretch, extend, direct'. Its past participle tensus gives tense and tension.
items.cn: tendere 意为“伸展、延伸、指向”。其过去分词 tensus 生成 tense 与 tension。

items.en: tendere is traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch', the same root behind tendon and the ten- of intend and extend.
items.cn: tendere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”，同一词根见于 tendon，以及 intend、extend 中的 ten-。

items.en: The 'care for' sense comes from attend, 'to direct the mind to', later shortened to tend in everyday use.
items.cn: “照料”义出自 attend“把心思朝向”，后在日常使用中缩略为 tend。

items.en: attendere is ad- 'to' plus tendere 'stretch': to stretch one's mind toward something. So care and inclination are distant cousins after all.
items.cn: attendere 是 ad-“朝向”加 tendere“伸展”：把心思朝某物伸去。故“照料”与“倾向”终究是远亲。

items.en: Modern English keeps both: tend to do (incline) and tend a fire (care for). Context, not spelling, tells them apart.
items.cn: 现代英语两者皆存：tend to do（倾向）与 tend a fire（照看）。区分靠语境，不靠拼写。

note.en: The first group is the tend family and its look-alikes; the second is verbs that share either the leaning or the caring sense.
note.cn: 第一组是 tend 词族与形近词；第二组是共享“倾斜”或“照料”义的动词。

entries.definition: a regular inclination to behave in a certain way.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式行事的经常性倾向。

entries.definition: expressing a strong biased point of view. It comes from German Tendenz, not directly from English tend.
entries.definitionCN: 表达强烈偏见的。出自德语 Tendenz，并非直接来自英语 tend。

entries.definition: looking after; the act of caring for.
to lean or be disposed toward something. It is more formal and more spatial than tend.
entries.definitionCN: 向某物倾斜或有意向。比 tend 更正式、更空间化。

entries.definition: to look after someone's needs. It is the plain phrase for the 'tend' care sense.
entries.definitionCN: 照看某人的需要。是“照料”义的朴素说法。

entries.definition: to be drawn toward something as if by gravity. It stresses attraction rather than habit.
entries.definitionCN: 如受重力吸引般趋向某物。强调吸引而非习惯。

normalIntro.en: Real links: tendere 'stretch', attend shortened to tend, the tense/tension family, and the two-verb history.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tendere“伸展”、attend 缩略为 tend、tense 与 tension 词族，以及“双动词”历史。

normal.en: Tendere means 'stretch'. Behaviour tends when it stretches toward one outcome rather than another.
normal.cn: tendere 意为“伸展”。行为 tend，就是朝某个结果而非另一个伸展。

normal.en: The care sense is attend shortened: to tend a patient is to stretch your attention toward them.
normal.cn: 照料义是 attend 的缩略：tend 病人，就是把注意力朝他们伸去。

normal.en: Tend, tense, tension, tendon all go back to stretching. A tendon is a stretched cord.
normal.cn: tend、tense、tension、tendon 都回到“伸展”。肌腱就是一根被拉紧的索。

normal.en: Tend to do = habit leans; tend a fire = attention stays. Context decides which verb you met.
normal.cn: tend to do 是习惯倾斜；tend a fire 是注意力留守。语境决定你遇到哪一个。

normal.en: Intend and extend hide the same ten-: stretching the mind toward, or stretching out.
normal.cn: intend 与 extend 藏着同一个 ten-：把心思伸向，或向外伸展。

abstract.en: A tendency is a future written into the present as a slope; tend names the slope without promising the destination.
abstract.cn: 倾向是写进当下的未来，形如斜坡；tend 命名坡度，却不承诺终点。

abstract.en: Care and inclination meet in attention: both are a stretching of the self toward something beyond it.
abstract.cn: 照料与倾向在“注意”处相遇：两者都是自我朝外物的伸展。

abstract.en: What we tend grows; what we merely intend does not. The hand matters more than the plan.
abstract.cn: 我们所照料的东西会生长；仅仅所意图的不会。手比计划更重要。

examples.en: Prices tend to rise before the holiday.
examples.cn: 节前价格往往上涨。

examples.en: A nurse tended him through the night.
examples.cn: 一名护士整夜照料他。

examples.en: The discussion tended toward the question of cost.
examples.cn: 讨论逐渐转向成本问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “探的”——探着身子往一个方向去，也探身照看病人 → tend 倾向、照料

root: 两个来源合流：“倾向”义出自拉丁 tendere“伸展”（经古法语 tendre）；“照料”义是 attend 的缩略，出自拉丁 attendere“留心”（ad- + tendere）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of tend, split between two histories: a stretching toward (inclination, direction, convergence) and an attention turned toward (care, herding, service). Both are forms of leaning out of oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: tend 的九个义项分属两段历史：朝某物伸展（倾向、方向、收敛）与把注意转向某物（照料、放牧、服侍）。两者都是自我向外倾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line stretched toward a point, and a herder's gaze stretched toward a flock.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条朝某点伸展的线，与牧人朝羊群伸去的目光。

branches.en: HABIT: behaviour leans in a predictable direction.
branches.cn: 习惯：行为朝可预测的方向倾斜。

branches.en: DIRECTION AND LIMIT: paths and sequences stretch toward a point.
branches.cn: 方向与极限：路径与序列朝某点伸展。

branches.en: CARE: attention is turned toward a person, a fire, or a machine that needs upkeep.
branches.cn: 照料：注意力转向需要维护的人、炉火或机器。

branches.en: SERVICE: bars, flocks, and lords are all kept by a presence that stays.
branches.cn: 服侍：酒吧、羊群与领主，都靠一种留守的在场维持。

branches.en: THE UNFINISHED MIND: a group can tend toward a view without having reached it.
branches.cn: 未完成的心智：群体可以趋向某观点而尚未抵达。

intro.en: Tend's English family splits along its two origins: tendency belongs to the 'stretch' verb, while attend and its derivatives belong to the 'heed' verb. The ten- root also gives tense, tension, tendon, intend, and extend.
intro.cn: tend 的英语词族沿两个来源分裂：tendency 属“伸展”动词，attend 及其派生属“留心”动词。ten- 词根还给出 tense、tension、tendon、intend、extend。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere 'stretch' has the participle tensus, source of tense and tension. Latin attendere 'stretch toward' is ad- plus tendere, and its French shortening gave the care sense of tend. The same *ten- root underlies tendon.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tendere“伸展”的分词 tensus 是 tense 与 tension 的来源。拉丁 attendere“朝…伸展”是 ad- 加 tendere，其法语缩略给出 tend 的照料义。同一 *ten- 词根支撑 tendon。

items.meaningCN: 照料中的；趋向的（现在分词）
有倾向性的；带偏见的（形容词）

items.meaning: to be present at; to give heed
to stretch the mind toward; to plan
the state of being stretched; strain

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch the mind toward; heed

definition_en: a leaning or inclination toward a particular kind of behaviour, direction or outcome
core_image: 一枚小球放在微微倾斜的桌面上，手一松，它总是往同一个方向滚
scene: 议事厅里，同一批人每次表决都往同一个方向靠，连反对者也渐渐跟着举手。There was a clear tendency for the committee to side with the older members.
sceneCN: 这里本词指群体在反复选择中表现出的固定偏向（第 1 个义项：一般倾向）；句意为委员会明显倾向于站在年长成员一边。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到动词，语义为「趋向；倾向」
由同一词根加表「带有倾向」的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「有偏向的」
由上一形容词加副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「带有偏向地」
由上一形容词加名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「偏向性」

senses.title: A general leaning
senses.definition: a general leaning of people or things toward one kind of behaviour or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物总体上偏向某一类行为或结果的态势
senses.example: There is a general tendency for prices to rise before holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 节前价格上涨存在一种普遍倾向。
senses.why: The word began as a stretched direction, and the first sense is that leaning seen in a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 本词最初指被拉伸的方向，第一个义项就是整个群体表现出的这种偏向。

senses.title: A personal habit of mind
senses.definition: a person's habitual inclination to act or feel in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在行为或感受上习惯性的偏向
senses.example: She has a tendency to interrupt when she is nervous.
senses.exampleCN: 她紧张时有打断别人的癖性。
senses.why: A single person also leans one way again and again, and the word names that private tilt.
senses.whyCN: 单个人也会一次次往同一侧倾，本词就指这种私人的偏向。

senses.title: A statistical movement
senses.definition: the direction in which a set of figures moves over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一组数据在一段时间内变动的方向
senses.example: The figures show an upward tendency in household savings.
senses.exampleCN: 数据显示家庭储蓄呈上升趋势。
senses.why: Numbers plotted over time lean visibly, and that lean is what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 按时间画出的数据会显出倾斜，本词描述的正是这种倾斜。

senses.title: A current of opinion
senses.definition: a broad drift of opinion or policy in a society at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期社会舆论或政策上广泛出现的走向
senses.example: A reformist tendency gained ground among younger voters.
senses.exampleCN: 改革倾向在年轻选民中占了上风。
senses.why: When many minds lean together, the lean becomes a public current rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人的心思同时倾斜，这种倾斜就成了公共潮流而非私人情绪。

senses.title: A physical drift
senses.definition: the direction in which a body or substance naturally moves or changes
senses.definitionCN: 物体或物质自然移动或变化的方向
senses.example: Hot air has a tendency to rise above cooler air.
senses.exampleCN: 热空气有升到冷空气之上的趋向。
senses.why: The oldest image is physical: something stretched or pulled toward a point.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是物理性的：某物被拉向某一点。

senses.title: A medical susceptibility
senses.definition: a bodily weakness that makes a person likely to develop a particular illness
senses.definitionCN: 身体上的弱点使人容易患上某种疾病
senses.example: The condition runs in families with a tendency to low bone density.
senses.exampleCN: 该病多见于有骨密度偏低易感性的家族。
senses.why: A body leaning toward illness is described with the same word as any other lean.
senses.whyCN: 身体向疾病倾斜，用的仍是与其它倾斜相同的词。

senses.title: A stylistic leaning in art
senses.definition: a recurring preference for certain forms or moods in an artist's work
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家作品中反复出现的对某些形式或情绪的偏好
senses.example: His later novels show a tendency toward long, quiet scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 他后期的小说显出偏爱篇幅长而安静的场景。
senses.why: Style is a repeated lean of the hand, and critics borrowed the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 风格是手反复倾斜的结果，评论者便借用这个词来指它。

senses.title: A market drift
senses.definition: the direction in which prices or demand appear to be heading
senses.definitionCN: 价格或需求看起来正在走向的方向
senses.example: Traders watched the tendency of the index for the week.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员盯着这一周指数的走势。
senses.why: Markets are read as leaning one way, so forecasters speak of a tendency rather than a certainty.
senses.whyCN: 市场被看作正在往一侧倾，故预测者说倾向而不说定论。

intro.en: Tendency comes from the Latin verb for stretching or aiming, through a medieval Latin noun for a leaning; it is not related to the word for a trend, which comes from an Old English verb for turning.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，经中世纪拉丁语表「倾斜」的名词进入英语；它与表「走势」的那个词并不同源，后者出自古英语中表「转动」的动词。

items.en: The verb meant to stretch out, hold out or aim, and the image is a body or a line extended toward a point.
items.cn: 这一拉丁动词意为「伸出、朝向、瞄准」，意象是身体或线条朝某一点展开。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed a noun from the participle of that verb, naming a leaning or an inclination.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用该动词的分词造出名词，指倾斜或倾向。

items.en: English took the noun in the seventeenth century for a leaning of mind, body or fortune.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该名词，指心思、身体或运势上的偏向。

items.en: The word for a trend is not a relative: it comes from an Old English verb meaning to turn or revolve, and only later came to mean a direction.
items.cn: 表「走势」的那个词并非同族：它出自古英语中表「转动、旋转」的动词，后来才引申为方向。

items.en: Source uncertain: the older shape of the Latin verb is generally reconstructed, and the first English citation of the noun is not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一拉丁动词的更早形态一般为重构，该名词在英语中的最早书证年代亦无确说。

note.en: Group one collects forms that look or sound close to this noun; group two collects words for leanings of mind or body.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的形式；第二组是表示心思或身体偏向的词。

entries.definition: A true relative: the verb means to be inclined or to take care of, and the noun adds a suffix of state.
entries.definitionCN: 确为同源：动词表示趋向或照管，名词则加上表状态的后缀。

entries.definition: It means pushing a one-sided view, built on the same leaning root with an adjective suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 意为推行片面观点，由同一表「倾斜」的词根加形容词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Often treated as a synonym but a different word: it comes from an Old English verb for turning, not from the Latin verb for stretching, so the two are not cognate.
entries.definitionCN: 常被当作同义词，其实是另一个词：它出自古英语表「转动」的动词，而非拉丁语表「伸展」的动词，二者并无同源关系。

entries.definition: It sounds almost the same but comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold, and it names the right to occupy property rather than a leaning.
entries.definitionCN: 读音几乎相同，却出自拉丁语表「握持」的动词，指占用房产的权利，与偏向无关。

entries.definition: A leaning of mind or body, closer to a settled preference than to a measured direction in figures.
entries.definitionCN: 心思或身体上的倾斜，更接近固定的偏好，而非数据中被测量的方向。

entries.definition: A strong natural tendency to behave in a particular way, usually toward something undesirable.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈而天生的行为偏向，通常指向不受欢迎的事。

entries.definition: A person's habitual temperament, the whole cast of mind rather than one lean.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人习惯的性情，是整个心性而非单一偏向。

entries.definition: A slow general movement or change of opinion, stressing gradual motion rather than a built-in lean.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的整体移动或舆论变化，强调渐进，而非内在的倾斜。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant to stretch: a line pulled toward a point, and that is the image of the whole family.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为伸展：一条被拉向某点的线，这就是整个词族的意象。

normal.en: The family runs tendency, tend, tendentious, tendentiously, tendentiousness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括倾向、趋向、有偏向的、带有偏向地与偏向性。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a tendency to overreact, a downward tendency, a growing tendency.
normal.cn: 固定说法：过度反应的倾向、下降趋势、日益增长的趋势。

normal.en: Keep it apart from the word for a trend: that one came from an old verb for turning, not from stretching.
normal.cn: 要与表「走势」的那个词分开：后者出自表「转动」的古动词，并非出自「伸展」。

normal.en: Statistics speak of a tendency when a line on a chart slants; medicine speaks of one when a body is likely to fall ill.
normal.cn: 统计学说倾向，是指图表上的线出现斜度；医学说倾向，是指身体容易生病。

abstract.en: Picture a metal ball rolling toward the low edge of a tilted table, again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗金属球一次次滚向倾斜桌面的低边。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting toward one side of a square without anyone giving an order.
abstract.cn: 想象人群没有接到任何指令，却慢慢移向广场的一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that always reaches for the same pen, even when another lies closer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手总去拿同一支笔，哪怕另一支离得更近。

examples.en: Prices show a tendency to fall after the harvest.
examples.cn: 收成之后价格显出下跌的倾向。

examples.en: He has a tendency to talk over people in meetings.
examples.cn: 他在会上有抢别人话头的癖性。

examples.en: The survey found a tendency toward smaller households.
examples.cn: 调查发现家庭规模有变小的趋势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「伸展」记成一条被拉向某处的线：线往哪边斜，就是往哪边倾向。

root: 来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，中世纪拉丁语由其分词构成表「倾斜」的名词，英语借入后指各种偏向；与表「走势」的词不同源，后者出自古英语表「转动」的动词；更深来源一般为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one model: a line or a body stretched toward one point, so that it leans the same way each time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个模型展开：一条线或一具身体被拉向某一点，于是每次都往同一侧倾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball on a tilted table, always rolling to the same low corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：倾斜桌面上的球，总滚向同一个低角。

branches.en: LEANING LINE: the general lean of people and the physical drift of matter share one image of a stretched line.
branches.cn: 倾斜的线：人群的整体偏向与物质的物理趋向共享「被拉长的线」这一意象。

branches.en: PRIVATE LEAN: one person's repeated tilt becomes a habit of mind.
branches.cn: 私人偏向：一个人反复的倾斜成为心理习性。

branches.en: MEASURED SLANT: charts and markets are read as leaning, so the word names a direction in figures.
branches.cn: 可测的斜度：图表与市场都被读作倾斜，本词于是指数据中的方向。

branches.en: PUBLIC CURRENT: many minds leaning together become a drift of opinion.
branches.cn: 公共潮流：许多心思同时倾斜，便成舆论走向。

branches.en: BODY AND ART: a body likely to fall ill and a hand that prefers certain forms both lean in the same old sense.
branches.cn: 身体与艺术：易患病的身体与偏爱某些形式的手，都在同一古老意义上倾斜。

intro.en: The noun is built from a Latin verb and a suffix of state, and English keeps a small family around it, so the word can be read in parts.
intro.cn: 这个名词由拉丁语动词加表状态的后缀构成，英语周围还保留少量同族词，因此可以按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb supplies the stretching, the Latin participle supplies the leaning, and English supplies only the closing noun suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词提供「伸展」，拉丁语分词提供「倾斜」，英语只提供收尾的名词后缀。

items.example: The root shows in extend, intend and tension, all about stretching.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根见于延伸、打算、张力等词，都与伸展有关。

items.example: A bowstring is stretched, and so is a plan toward its aim.
items.exampleCN: 弓弦被拉紧，计划也朝目标伸展。

items.example: The participle describes what is already leaning.
items.exampleCN: 这一分词描述已经在倾斜的东西。

items.structure: tendens plus a medieval Latin noun suffix
items.example: The medieval noun turned the act of leaning into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪名词把倾斜这一动作变成一种事物。

items.meaning: a leaning toward a kind of act or outcome
items.example: A tendency can be measured over many cases.
items.exampleCN: 倾向可以在许多个案上被测量出来。

items.example: The report was tendentious from its first line.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告从第一行起就带有偏向。

items.meaning: the quality of pushing a lean
items.example: Readers objected to the tendentiousness of the piece.
items.exampleCN: 读者反对这篇文章的偏向性。

items.structure: Latin prefix plus the root tend-
items.example: They extended the deadline by a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们把截止期限延长了一周。

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch, to extend, to aim

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到动词，语义为「趋向；倾向」
由同一词根加表「带有倾向」的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「有偏向的」
由上一形容词加副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「带有偏向地」
由上一形容词加名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「偏向性」

definition_en: a game in which two or four players hit a ball over a net using rackets
core_image: 一张球网隔开两人：球被球拍来回击打过网
scene: 周末清晨，球拍击球的脆响在球场回荡，汗水洒在红色的地面上。We played tennis on the clay court until noon.
sceneCN: 这里 tennis 是「网球运动」（第 1 个义项：一种隔网用球拍击球的球类运动）；句意是我们一直在红土网球场上打球打到中午。

derivatives.zh: table + tennis 复合词，义为「乒乓球」，缩小版网球运动
tennis + elbow 复合词，义为「网球肘」，一种常见于网球运动员的肘部劳损

senses.title: The sport of hitting a ball over a net
senses.definition: a game in which two or four players use rackets to hit a ball back and forth over a net
senses.definitionCN: 由两名或四名运动员用球拍隔着球网来回击球的球类运动
senses.example: She plays tennis every weekend with her sister.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个周末都和姐姐一起打网球。
senses.why: The core image is the net splitting two sides and the ball flying back and forth; the sport itself is named by this single image.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一张网隔开两方、球在空中来回飞：这项运动本身就用这一个画面命名，因此最基本义就是「网球运动」。

senses.title: The ball used in the game
senses.definition: the soft yellow-green ball used in the game of tennis
senses.definitionCN: 打网球所用的黄绿色软球
senses.example: A stray tennis rolled under the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 一个网球滚到了栅栏底下。
senses.why: The name of the game easily transfers to the object the game is played with; the sport lends its name to its ball.
senses.whyCN: 运动的名字很容易转指这项运动所用的器具：运动的名称借给了它使用的球，于是 tennis 也可指「网球（球本身）」。

senses.title: A tennis session or match occasion
senses.definition: an occasion or period of playing tennis
senses.definitionCN: 打网球的一次活动或时段
senses.example: Let's have a quick tennis before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午餐前我们快点打一场网球吧。
senses.why: Activities are often named without articles in English; the sport name becomes shorthand for one occasion of playing it.
senses.whyCN: 英语里活动名称常可省去冠词直接代指活动本身：运动名成为「打一次」的简称，义为一场网球活动。

senses.title: Tennis as a competitive professional world
senses.definition: the professional world or circuit of tennis competitions
senses.definitionCN: 职业网球赛事构成的世界或圈子
senses.example: She has spent a decade in professional tennis.
senses.exampleCN: 她在职业网坛已打拼了十年。
senses.why: A sport name can stand for the whole community and circuit built around it; playing becomes a career field.
senses.whyCN: 运动名称可代指围绕它建立的全部社群与赛事体系：打球变成一种职业领域，即「网坛」。

senses.title: Tennis as a school or club subject
senses.definition: tennis taught or organized as a course or club activity
senses.definitionCN: 作为课程或社团活动开设的网球项目
senses.example: Tennis is offered as an elective this term.
senses.exampleCN: 本学期开设网球选修课。
senses.why: Institutions name their offerings after the sport; the game becomes a labeled program within school or club life.
senses.whyCN: 学校与俱乐部用运动名来命名所开设的项目：网球运动成为课程表上的一个标签，即「网球课/项目」。

senses.title: Table tennis as a compound
senses.definition: used in compounds such as table tennis for similar net games
senses.definitionCN: 用于 table tennis 等复合词，指类似的隔网球类运动
senses.example: They watched table tennis on television.
senses.exampleCN: 他们看电视转播的乒乓球比赛。
senses.why: The image of hitting a ball over a net is copied at table size; the name travels into smaller versions of the game.
senses.whyCN: 隔网击球的画面被缩小到桌面上：这一运动名迁移到迷你版本，构成「乒乓球」等复合词。

senses.title: A tennis court or facility context
senses.definition: used to label courts, clubs, and equipment for the game
senses.definitionCN: 用于标注网球场、网球俱乐部及器材
senses.example: The tennis club opens at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 网球俱乐部九点开门。
senses.why: Facilities take the sport's name as a label; the game name marks the places where it is played.
senses.whyCN: 场地设施借运动名作标签：运动的名字标记了这项运动进行的场所。

senses.title: Historic real tennis as the original form
senses.titleCN: 历史用法：古式室内网球
senses.definition: real tennis, the older indoor form of the game played in royal courts
senses.definitionCN: real tennis，指起源于宫廷的旧式室内网球
senses.example: Real tennis survives in a few old courts in England.
senses.exampleCN: 古式网球仍在英国少数老球场存续。
senses.why: Before modern lawns, the game was played in walled courts; the historic form keeps the oldest sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 现代草地球场出现之前，这项运动在四壁围合的宫廷球场进行：历史形态保留了该词最古老的义项。

senses.title: Figurative back-and-forth exchange
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：来回往复的交锋
senses.definition: a situation of actions or words going back and forth like a tennis rally
senses.definitionCN: 比喻言行像网球对打一样来回往复的局面
senses.example: The lawyers kept a tennis of objections and replies.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们你来我往， objections 与答辩不断交锋。
senses.why: The rally image of a ball flying back and forth maps onto any exchange of actions; the game becomes a metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 球来回对打的画面可以映射到任何往复的互动：运动名变成比喻，指你来我往的交锋。

intro.en: Tennis has an unusual etymology: it entered English from Old French as a shout used in the medieval ball game.
intro.cn: tennis 的词源颇为特别：它以中世纪球戏中的喊叫声身份从古法语进入英语。

items.en: The word is generally traced to Old French tenez, meaning hold, receive, the call made when serving the ball.
items.cn: 一般追溯至古法语 tenez（意为「接住、拿着」），是发球时的喊话。

items.en: The name appears in Middle English for the royal court game played indoors with the palm first, then rackets.
items.cn: 中古英语时期该词指宫廷室内球戏，最初徒手击球，后来改用球拍。

items.en: Rackets replaced the bare hand, and the game moved between indoor courts and open play.
items.cn: 球拍取代了徒手击球，游戏在室内球场与露天场地之间流转。

items.en: Modern lawn tennis was codified in the 1870s, giving the word its dominant present meaning.
items.cn: 现代草地网球于十九世纪七十年代定型，赋予了 tennis 如今的主导含义。

items.en: Today tennis means the global racket sport, its ball, and its professional world.
items.cn: 如今 tennis 指全球性的球拍运动、网球本身以及职业网坛。

note.en: Tennis is mostly a unique noun, but compounds and neighboring game words cause confusion.
note.cn: tennis 是较为独特的名词，但复合词与邻近的球类词汇容易造成混淆。

entries.definition: a principle or belief held by a group
entries.definitionCN: 信条、原则。只是拼写相近，词源不同
打网球用的黄绿色球，tennis 的复合名词

entries.definition: the marked court where tennis is played
entries.definitionCN: 网球场，tennis 的复合名词

entries.definition: a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a net
entries.definitionCN: 用羽毛球隔网对打的球拍运动，与网球同类

entries.definition: a team game hitting a ball over a net without rackets
entries.definitionCN: 不用球拍、团队隔网击球的排球运动

entries.definition: a racket game hitting a ball against walls in an enclosed court
entries.definitionCN: 在封闭球场向墙壁击球的壁球运动

normalIntro.en: Use the serve-call origin and common compounds to remember tennis.
normalIntro.cn: 利用发球喊叫的来源和常见复合词来记忆 tennis。

normal.en: Tennis comes from Old French tenez, meaning take it: the server's shout before hitting the ball.
normal.cn: tennis 来自古法语 tenez（接住）：发球者击球前的喊话。

normal.en: Table tennis means table-size tennis: same net image, smaller court.
normal.cn: table tennis（乒乓球）：桌面版的 tennis，同样的隔网画面，更小的场地。

normal.en: A tennis court, a tennis racket, a tennis match: the word labels the whole gear set.
normal.cn: tennis court、tennis racket、tennis match：这个词为整套装备与场合打标签。

normal.en: Wimbledon is the most famous tennis tournament; champions become household names.
normal.cn: 温布尔登是最著名的网球赛事；冠军家喻户晓。

normal.en: Real tennis is the medieval indoor ancestor of modern tennis.
normal.cn: real tennis（古式网球）是现代网球的中世纪室内祖先。

abstract.en: Hear the old server shout tenez before each serve, and the name sticks to the game.
abstract.cn: 想象每次发球前老球员喊一声 tenez，名字便贴在了这项运动上。

abstract.en: Picture a yellow-green ball flying back and forth, drawing an arc over the net.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗黄绿色的球来回飞舞，在球网上空划出弧线。

abstract.en: Feel the rhythm of a rally: hit, reply, hit, like a conversation across the net.
abstract.cn: 感受对打的节奏：击球、回击、再击球，像隔着球网在对话。

examples.en: She won the tennis final in three straight sets.
examples.cn: 她直落三盘赢下网球决赛。

examples.en: The kids hit a tennis against the garage wall all afternoon.
examples.cn: 孩子们整个下午对着车库墙打网球。

examples.en: Their debate turned into a tennis of arguments and counterarguments.
examples.cn: 他们的辩论变成了你来我往的交锋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 tennis 」谐音「忒耐死」——打网球忒累，耐力不足可不行。

root: tennis 一般认为源自古法语 tenez（tenir「拿、接」的命令式），是中世纪发球时的喊话「接住！」；词形先指宫廷室内球戏，十九世纪随草地网球定型为现代义。来源说法主流可靠，个别细节（何时由喊叫转成运动名）属一般推断。

sensesIntro.en: Tennis radiates from the sport itself to its ball, a playing occasion, the professional world, compounds, and metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: tennis 从运动本身辐射到网球用球、一次打球活动、职业网坛、复合词用法与比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball flying back and forth over a net between two sides
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗球隔着球网在两方之间来回飞舞

branches.en: The net game itself, from medieval courts to modern lawns
branches.cn: 隔网球戏本身，从中世纪宫廷到现代草地

branches.en: The name lends itself to the ball of the game
branches.cn: 运动名将自身借给它使用的球

branches.en: Play occasions, courses, and facilities take the sport's name
branches.cn: 打球活动、课程与场地设施借用运动之名

branches.en: The whole professional circuit is named by the sport
branches.cn: 整个职业赛事体系以运动名代指

branches.en: The net image copies into compounds and back-and-forth metaphors
branches.cn: 隔网画面复制为复合词与往复交锋的比喻

intro.en: Tennis is a borrowed single word, but it forms many compounds and sport-family terms.
intro.cn: tennis 是借入的单词，但构成了大量复合词与球类运动家族词。

latinIntro.en: Tennis has no Latin relatives; it comes from Old French tenez, from Latin tenere at one further remove.
latinIntro.cn: tennis 没有直接的拉丁同源词；它来自古法语 tenez，间接可追至拉丁语 tenere。

items.example: Tenez! The server called before hitting.
items.exampleCN: 发球者击球前喊道：「接住！」

items.example: tenir la balle, to hold the ball
Latin tenere survives in contain and retain
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 tenere 留存于 contain、retain 之中

items.example: They played table tennis after dinner.
items.exampleCN: 晚饭后他们打了乒乓球。

items.example: The tennis court was freshly lined.
She strung her tennis racket tightly.
items.exampleCN: 她把网球拍的线绷得很紧。

items.example: A tennis ball bounced over the fence.

items.exampleCN: 那位网球运动员每天训练。

items.example: Real tennis is played at Hampton Court.
items.exampleCN: 汉普顿宫仍在进行古式网球。
草地网球始于十九世纪七十年代。
